commit.message:
docs: stop presenting deprecated features as current on the spec overview pages (#3552)

The architecture and base protocol overview pages are where many people
new to MCP start. Both still presented sampling, roots and logging as
current features, with no indication that they are deprecated as of
`2026-07-28` (SEP-2577).

Fixes #3548

## Architecture page

Builds on the branch Lazzaretti proposed in #3548 (their commit is
included as-is), which updates the five places the issue lists:

- Intro: "context exchange and sampling coordination" becomes "context
exchange"
- Host: "Coordinates AI/LLM integration and sampling" becomes
"Coordinates AI/LLM integration"
- Servers: elicitation is the example of client input
- Capability Negotiation: clients "declare capabilities like elicitation
handling"
- Sequence diagram: the `InputRequiredResult` example is
`elicitation/create`, with the host asking the user for input

On top of that, the Servers bullet reads "Request client input (e.g.
elicitation)" and carries a footnote saying sampling and roots requests
are also delivered via `InputRequiredResult` but are deprecated and
should not be used in new implementations, linking to the Deprecated
Features registry.

## Base protocol overview

- Client Features: "Elicitation provided by clients; sampling and root
directory lists are deprecated", linking to the registry
- Utilities: examples are argument completion and pagination, followed
by "logging is deprecated", linking to the registry
- Message Patterns: the MRTR summary uses "(e.g. elicitation)" as its
example of client input

The component list is an enumeration, so the deprecated features stay
listed and are labelled inline. The architecture page only gives an
example, so there they move to a footnote.

## Released revision

The same changes are applied to the `2026-07-28` copies of both pages,
which were identical to draft apart from link paths. Links there point
at the `2026-07-28` pages.

## Not included

The reserved `_meta` key tables on the base protocol overview still list
`io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` without a deprecation marker. Those
rows link to the Logging page, which carries the deprecation notice.

## Verification

- `npm run prep` passes
- Footnote syntax is already rendered by the docs site on the SEP pages
(for example SEP-2567), and the generated "Footnotes" heading does not
appear in the table of contents

---------

Co-authored-by: Fabrizio Lazzaretti <fabrizio@lazzaretti.me>

commit.message:
feat(blog): draw a share card for every post (#3553)

Every page on the blog shared one static `og-image.png`: the wordmark on
a dark ground. This draws a share card for each post at build time and
fills in the image metadata that was missing.

## The card

A 1200x630 PNG on the blog's dark ground. It carries the blog's name,
the post's title, its date, and its authors one to a line. There is no
description on it.

The lower right corner holds a pattern of ten evenly spaced diagonal
stripes. Four wavy lines cross the field and cut the stripes they meet,
and every cut leaves a gap of the same size. A wave skips some stripes,
so some pieces run long and some are short. A few pieces are white and
the rest are two greys. Where the waves fall, which stripes they skip
and which pieces are white all follow from the post's file name, so
every post gets a pattern of its own and keeps it from build to build.

Pages that are not posts (home, tags, archives, 404) share one card that
carries the site's description.

A post that sets `cover.image` or `images` in front matter still gets
its own picture, as before.

## How it is made

Hugo draws the cards itself, in `layouts/partials/og/image.html`. There
is no build step outside Hugo, no new dependency, and no workflow
change. A new post gets its card without anyone making one. The cards
land at `/og/<file name>.png`.

Things a reviewer might not expect:

- Hugo cannot draw shapes. Each piece of stripe is cut from a picture of
one long stripe (`assets/og/stripe-*.png`): the left part gives the
piece its lower end, the right part its upper end, and the two are laid
side by side.
- Hugo's text filter has no letter spacing and breaks a line only when
it is full. So the title uses a copy of Geist SemiBold with 30 units
taken off every advance width (the blog's -0.03em), and the partial
breaks the title's lines itself, evenly, from a table of character
widths (`assets/og/advances.json`).
- `assets/og/README.md` says how every picture and font in that folder
was made, with the script for the fonts.
- A cold build of the whole site takes about 8 seconds on my machine, up
from under 1. Hugo caches the cards in `resources/_gen`, so later local
builds are fast.
- `static/og-image.png` and `params.images` are removed. The old URL
`https://blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/og-image.png` stops resolving, so
links already shared keep their cached preview only until the platform
refetches.

## Metadata

- `og:image` now comes with `og:image:type`, `og:image:width`,
`og:image:height` and `og:image:alt`.
- `twitter:image:alt` is added.
- Posts get one `article:author` per author.
- The JSON-LD `image` of a post points at its card.

## Testing

- Production `hugo` build completes without errors or warnings and
writes 30 cards: 29 posts and the shared one.
- Looked at every card in a contact sheet: short, long and very long
titles, one to nine authors (more than four are cut to three and "and N
more").
- Checked the emitted tags on a post, the home page and the tags page.
- `prettier --check` passes on the new README and the archetype. The
full `npm run prep` was not run; the change touches no docs, schema or
SEP files.

To see the cards, open `/og/site.png` or `/og/mcp-release-cycle.png` on
the preview deployment.

commit.message:
feat(blog): open search in a dialog and even out the header buttons (#3551)

Two changes to the blog's header and search.

## Header buttons

The social icons sat in 32px boxes 4px apart, while search and the theme
switch were 40px boxes in their own grid columns with 16px gaps, so
those two stood about twice as far apart as the rest. All five are now
one row of 32px boxes with 4px gaps, in the same order. On phones the
two-row layout is unchanged, but every button is 40px with no gap, so
both rows step evenly.

## Search

Search no longer has a page of its own. The header's search button, `/`,
or Ctrl+K (⌘K on a Mac) opens a native modal `<dialog>` over the page
the reader is on.

- Before anything is typed it lists the four most recent posts.
- Results are laid out like the post list: the date in a column of its
own, then the title with up to two lines of the summary or of the
passage that matched, the typed words in ink. On phones the date moves
above the title. Results used to be titles only.
- Focus stays in the field. The arrow keys move a highlight, Enter opens
it, Esc closes the dialog and returns focus to the button.
- Fuse, the search script and the index load only when the reader
hovers, focuses or opens search.
- On phones the dialog takes nearly the full screen and the Esc chip
becomes a "Close" button.

Things a reviewer might not expect:

- `/search/` is removed (`content/search.md` and its layout), along with
the Search entry in the menu config. The old URL now returns the 404
page, whose text no longer links to it.
- The search index gains `date` and `tags`, and its text is
HTML-unescaped so entities such as `’` don't show up in results.
- Matching is slightly stricter: the fuzzy threshold goes from 0.4 to
0.3, and titles and tags weigh more than body text.
- Without JavaScript the search button is hidden, like the theme switch.

## Testing

- Production `hugo` build completes without errors and emits no
`/search/` page.
- Checked in headless Edge against a local build: light, dark and phone
widths; opening by click, `/` and Ctrl+K; arrow keys and Enter; Esc
returning focus to the button; and that nothing of search loads before
the reader reaches for it.
- `npm run prep` was not run (no Node on the machine this was written
on). The change touches no Markdown, MDX, schema or SEP files.
